post.description:
List event tracker data with advanced filtering, sorting, and pagination.

This endpoint extends the company/list API functionality specifically for event tracker use cases.
It provides the same filtering, sorting, and pagination capabilities as the company API,
but with additional event-specific processing and risk-reward calculations.

## Event Tracker Specific Features

- **Event Enrichment**: Automatically adds `days_until_event` field to all events
- **Event Filtering**: Supports filtering by event properties using dot notation (e.g., `events.name`)
- **With Events Filter**: Use `with_events: true` to filter out companies that have no events
- **Next Event Computation**: Automatically computes `next_event` and `next_biggest_event` fields
- **Portfolio Integration**: Includes position exposure and P&L data for portfolio companies

## Request Parameters

- **with_events**: When `true`, filters out companies with no events. When `false` (default),
  returns all companies even if they have no events. This is useful for event-based filtering
  to avoid returning companies with empty event lists.

Get event tracker fields metadata, display information, and filterable values.

This endpoint provides comprehensive metadata about available event tracker fields, including
their descriptions, display types, and filterable capabilities. It serves as a data dictionary
for client applications to understand the available fields and their properties.

This endpoint extends the company/catalog API with event-specific fields and capabilities.
It includes all company fields plus additional event-related fields such as:
- Event information (name, date, description, etc.)
- Event types and impacts
- Event estimates and probabilities
- Next event and next biggest event computed fields

When building dynamic UI components, this endpoint enables applications to:
1. Discover all available event tracker fields and their display properties
2. Determine which fields support filtering operations
3. Retrieve the possible values for filterable fields to populate dropdown selectors
4. Get event-specific reference data (event types, impacts, probability bands)

## Query Parameters
- **include_filterable_values**: Boolean - When true, includes the complete list of unique
  values for each filterable string field. This allows client applications to populate
  selectors and dropdowns with available options.

## Usage Examples
- Get field definitions for UI rendering: POST /v2/event_tracker/catalog
- Get dropdown options for filters: POST /v2/event_tracker/catalog?include_filterable_values=true
- Get filtered options for a specific context: POST with filters to see only relevant values

post.description:
Get PnL metrics aggregated by sub-team.

Reads sub-team membership from the DuckDB mart table, then calculates
PnL metrics per sub-team. Per the AS5 PRD (Feature 2), each request
takes a single ``benchmark_id`` (default: XBI) which drives the
values in the single ``alpha`` column. The card's UI dropdown is
what changes ``benchmark_id``; the column header stays fixed as
``"alpha"`` regardless of selection.

Sub-team attribution uses **current composition only** — only
active members contribute to PnL. Former members are excluded from
both attribution and the response (the card surfaces no greyed-out
rows for them).

post.description:
List users with advanced filtering, sorting, and pagination.

This endpoint accepts a POST request with a JSON body containing filter criteria,
sorting preferences, and pagination parameters. It returns a paginated list of
users matching the criteria.

You can include related data like user roles by specifying them in the "includes" array.

## Request Body Structure

- **page**: Integer - Page number (starts at 1)
- **page_size**: Integer - Number of items per page (max 100)
- **sort_by**: String - Field to sort by (see UserSort enum for options)
- **sort_order**: String - Sort direction ("asc" or "desc")
- **includes**: Array - Related data to include in response
- **filter**: Object - Advanced filtering criteria
  - To search for text within user names, use a filter with field="first_name" or "last_name"
    and op="contains" or "icontains" (case insensitive)
  - To search by email, use a filter with field="email" and op="contains" or "icontains"
  - To filter by role name, include "role" in the includes parameter
    and use a filter with field="role.name" and op="eq" or "contains"
  - To search across multiple fields, use a logical "or" filter combining both conditions

## Filter System

The filter system supports comparison operators and logical operators:

### Comparison Operators
- eq: Equal
- gt: Greater than
- gte: Greater than or equal
- lt: Less than
- lte: Less than or equal
- contains: String contains
- icontains: Case-insensitive string contains
- starts_with: String starts with
- ends_with: String ends with
- is_null: Field is null

### Logical Operators
- and: All conditions must be true
- or: At least one condition must be true
- not: Negates the condition

### Structured Field Access
For fields that are part of a related object, use dot notation to access nested properties.

#### Role Fields
Fields for role:
- role.name: Name of the user's role
- role.description: Description of the user's role

```
Note: When filtering by a structured field, make sure to include the related object
in the "includes" array (e.g., include "role" when filtering by "role.name")

CompanyFilterField.title: CompanyFilterField
CompanyFilterField.description:
Available fields that can be used in company filter expressions.

This enum defines all the field names that can be used in filter conditions
to narrow down company results. It includes basic company properties and fields
from related entities (using dot notation).

## Basic Fields
These are direct properties of the company entity, for example:
- id: Company unique identifier
- name: Company name

## Related Entity Fields (Dot Notation)
These fields access properties of related entities, for example:
- primary_instrument.name: Name of the company's primary instrument
- primary_instrument.ticker: Ticker symbol of the company's primary instrument
- primary_analyst.name: Full name of the primary analyst
- secondary_analysts.name: Full name of any secondary analyst (list field)
- research_analysts.name: Full name of any research analyst (list field)
- venture_analyst.name: Full name of the venture analyst

## Special Fields
- analyst.name: Meta-field that searches across all analyst types
  (primary, secondary, research, and venture)

## Weighted Attribute Fields
- weighted_attributes.therapeutic_areas.value: Filter by therapeutic area tag value
- weighted_attributes.therapeutic_areas.weight: Filter by therapeutic area tag weight
- weighted_attributes.development_stages.value: Filter by development stage tag value
- weighted_attributes.development_stages.weight: Filter by development stage tag weight

## Automatic Data Loading
When filtering on a related field, the system automatically includes the necessary
data internally for processing, but the related fields will only be returned in
the response if explicitly requested in the "includes" parameter.

This model is used for the PATCH /v2/company/{company_id} endpoint to update
a company. Only the fields that are provided will be updated.

field.description: The user field to filter on (e.g., first_name, email)

op.description: Comparison operator to use (e.g., eq, gt, contains)

value.title: Value
value.description: Value to compare against (not required for is_null operator)

UserComparisonFilter.title: UserComparisonFilter
UserComparisonFilter.description: A filter that compares a user field to a value using an operator.

UserFilterField.title: UserFilterField
UserFilterField.description:
Fields that can be filtered on for users.

These fields can be used in comparison filters to narrow down user results.
Some fields require that the related data is included in the 'includes' parameter.

UserIncludes.title: UserIncludes
UserIncludes.description:
Related data that can be included in user responses.

These options allow you to specify which related data should be included
in the response. Including related data can be necessary for filtering
or sorting by those fields.

sort_by.description: Field to sort results by. When sorting by a relationship field, that relationship must be included in the 'includes' parameter.

includes.title: Includes
includes.description: Related data to include in the response

filter.title: Filter
filter.description: Advanced filtering criteria using comparison and logical operators. Use filters on the 'first_name', 'last_name', or 'email' fields for text search capabilities.

UserListRequest.title: UserListRequest
UserListRequest.description:
Request model for listing users with filtering, sorting and pagination.

This model is used for the POST /v2/user/list endpoint to provide
advanced filtering, sorting, and pagination options in the request body.

op.description: Logical operator to combine filters (and, or, not)

filters.title: Filters
filters.description: List of filters to combine. For 'not' operator, provide exactly one filter.

UserLogicalFilter.title: UserLogicalFilter
UserLogicalFilter.description: A filter that combines user filters using a logical operator.

UserSort.title: UserSort
UserSort.description:
Fields that can be used for sorting user results.

When sorting by a relationship field (like role),
that relationship must be included in the 'includes' parameter.

UserWithRelationshipsResponse.title: UserWithRelationshipsResponse
UserWithRelationshipsResponse.description: User response with optional related data.
